title: Finding a fraction of an amount
examples: How do I find a third of 15?
How do I find a fraction of a number?

explain.say: Siti has 15 marbles and gives one third to her brother. How many is that? Look at the board: the 15 marbles are shared into 3 equal groups, with 5 in each. One group is one third.

draw.text: Finding a fraction of an amount

explain.say: Remember, one third means one of 3 equal parts. This bar is cut into 3, and one part is shaded. So to find one third of 15, you share 15 into 3 equal groups. What do you think the bottom number tells you to do?
Yes: divide by the bottom number. 15 shared into 3 groups is 5 each. So one third of 15 is 5, and Siti gives her brother 5 marbles. How many does she keep?
What about two thirds? That is 2 of the 3 equal parts. See 2 parts shaded? One part of 15 is 5, so 2 parts are 10. Two thirds of 15 is 10. Divide by the bottom, then times by the top!
Excellent! Try a quarter of 20: share 20 into 4 groups, and each has 5. Wow: shops use this when they say a third off! Challenge: what is three quarters of 20?

faq.q: How do I find a third of 15?
faq.a: Share 15 into 3 equal groups. Each group has 5, so one third of 15 is 5.
First find one third: 15 divided by 3 is 5. Two thirds is 2 of those groups, so 2 times 5 is 10.

faq.q: How do I find a fraction of a number?
faq.a: Divide by the bottom number to find one part, then multiply by the top number. For three quarters of 20: 20 divided by 4 is 5, and 3 times 5 is 15.
asks: What is the rule for a fraction of an amount?

faq.q: Why do I divide by the bottom number?
faq.a: The bottom number says how many equal parts to share the amount into. Dividing finds the size of one part.

faq.q: What does a third off mean in a shop?
faq.a: It means the price drops by one third. A toy costing 30 with a third off is 10 cheaper, so you pay 20.

facts: One third of 15 is 5, and two thirds of 15 is 10.
To find a fraction of an amount, divide by the denominator and multiply by the numerator.

quiz.why: 12 shared into 4 equal groups is 3 each.

wrong.1: 4 is the number of groups, not the size of each.

quiz.why: 20 divided by 4 is 5, and 3 times 5 is 15.

wrong.2: 12 does not come from sharing 20 into quarters.
